# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 3

---

**3:1** But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them.

**3:2** In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was reckoned as a calamity,

**3:3** and their going from us was thought to be their destruction; but they are at peace.

**3:4** For though in the sight of others they were punished, their hope is full of immortality.

**3:5** Having been disciplined a little, they will receive great blessing; for God tested them and found them worthy of himself.

**3:6** Like gold in the furnace he proved them, and like a whole burnt offering he accepted them.

**3:7** In the time of their visitation they will shine forth, and will dart about like sparks through stubble.

**3:8** They will judge nations and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them forever.

**3:9** Those who trust in him will understand truth, and the faithful will abide with him in love; because grace and mercy are upon his holy ones, and he watches over his elect.

**3:10** But the ungodly will be punished as their reasoning deserves — those who disregarded righteousness and rebelled against the Lord.

**3:11** For whoever despises wisdom and instruction is utterly wretched; their hope is empty, their toils are futile, and their works are without value.

**3:12** Their wives are foolish and their children are depraved; their offspring is accursed.

**3:13** For blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who has not shared a bed in transgression; she shall have fruit at the visitation of souls.

**3:14** And blessed is the eunuch who has committed no transgression with his hands and has not entertained wicked thoughts against the Lord; for he will be granted especial favor for his faithfulness, and a most welcome place in the temple of the Lord.

**3:15** For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root of understanding never fails.

**3:16** But the children of adulterers will not reach maturity, and the offspring of an unlawful union will perish.

**3:17** For even if they live long they will be held in no esteem, and in the end their old age will be without honor.

**3:18** And if they die young, they will have neither hope nor consolation on the day of judgment.

**3:19** For the end of an unrighteous generation is grievous.

---

## Council Notes

**On 3:1 — the central verse:** All agents preserved "the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God" intact — this verse is too well-known and theologically precise to paraphrase. PNEUMA adds "held safe" but SOPHIA retains the bare form; the hand of God is itself the safety.

**On 3:3 — "catastrophe" vs. "destruction":** EMET "catastrophe," LOGOS/SOPHIA "destruction" — apōleia means utter ruin/destruction; "catastrophe" is anachronistic; "destruction" is more precise.

**On 3:6 — "whole burnt offering":** All agents retain holokautōma as "whole burnt offering." The sacrificial image is deliberate and must not be softened to "sacrifice."

**On 3:7 — "visitation":** SOPHIA retains episkopē as "visitation" across vv. 7 and 13. This semi-technical term (divine inspection/coming) is important theologically and must not be rendered generically.

**On 3:14 — the eunuch:** LOGOS and EMET give a close rendering; PNEUMA expands with contextual explanation. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's close rendering — the intertextual echo with Isa 56 is the reader's to perceive.

**On 3:19 — ponēra:** EMET "grievous," LOGOS "cruel," PNEUMA "pitiless." SOPHIA adopts "grievous" — most precise; ponēra means wretched/terrible without the specific emotional valence of "pitiless."
